title: E-Way Bill
outcomes: Determine when an e-way bill is required.
Explain Parts A and B, generation and validity.
Apply exemptions and consequences of non-compliance.

meta.exam_tip: Compute consignment value first (exclude exempt goods), then check special cases and exemptions.

concepts.title: When an e-way bill is required (s. 68, Rule 138)
body: Section 68 and Rule 138: an e-way bill is generated before movement of goods of consignment value exceeding ₹50,000 — in relation to a supply, for reasons other than supply (for example, sales returns), or due to inward supply from an unregistered person.
Consignment value is the invoice value including tax, excluding the value of exempt goods supplied on the same invoice.
Even below ₹50,000, it is required for inter-State movement by a principal to a job worker and inter-State movement of handicraft goods by persons exempt from registration.
concepts.analogy: The e-way bill is the electronic travel document that tells the tax system what is on the road.
concepts.work: A ₹60,000 invoice with ₹15,000 of exempt goods has a consignment value of ₹45,000 — no e-way bill.

concepts.title: Who generates it, Parts A and B, and validity
body: Part A (invoice details, GSTINs, HSN, value) is filled by the registered supplier or recipient who causes the movement; Part B (vehicle or transport document number) by whoever transports. Where the goods are handed to a transporter, he may fill Part B; the registered person may authorise the transporter to fill Part A too.

Validity: 1 day for each 200 km or part for normal cargo; 1 day for each 20 km for over-dimensional cargo. The first day runs till midnight of the following day. Validity can be extended within 8 hours before or after expiry if the goods could not reach in time due to exceptional circumstances.

An e-way bill may be cancelled within 24 hours if not verified in transit; the recipient may accept or reject it within 72 hours or before delivery, failing which it is deemed accepted. Transhipment needs Part B updated for each new vehicle.
concepts.analogy: Part A describes the goods; Part B tells where they are travelling and on what.
concepts.work: A truck that breaks down en route has its new vehicle number updated in Part B.

concepts.title: Exemptions, verification and consequences
body: Not required: goods in the Annexure (fresh fruits and vegetables, LPG for households, kerosene through PDS, jewellery and similar items); non-motorised conveyance; movement from port, airport, air cargo complex or land customs station to an inland container depot or container freight station for clearance, or under customs bond or seal; transit to or from Nepal or Bhutan; empty cargo containers; goods treated as no supply under Schedule III; movement of up to 20 km for weighment with a delivery challan; goods moved by defence formations.
Part B is not required where movement within the State is up to 50 km from the consignor's place to the transporter's place (or from the transporter's place to the consignee).

Rule 138B–138D and section 68(3): officers may intercept and verify; findings are uploaded within 24 hours (Part A) and the final report within 3 days. A transporter detained for over 30 minutes may report it on the portal.

Section 129: goods moving without valid documents may be detained or seized; they are released on payment of penalty — for the owner who comes forward, 200% of the tax payable (2% of value or ₹25,000, whichever is lower, for exempt goods); for others, the higher of 50% of the value and 200% of the tax (or 5% of value or ₹25,000 for exempt goods).
concepts.analogy: Exemptions cover low-risk goods and movements; missing paperwork on taxable goods is expensive.
concepts.work: Goods worth ₹2 lakh with tax of ₹36,000 caught without an e-way bill: the owner pays ₹72,000 penalty to release them.

illustrations.title: How long is it valid?
illustrations.q: Compute e-way bill validity: (a) normal cargo moving 450 km; (b) over-dimensional cargo moving 70 km. The bill for (a) was generated at 10:00 am on 3 June. When does day one end?

solution.text: A "day" ends at midnight of the next day after generation: the first day for (a) expires at midnight of 4 June, so validity of 3 days ends at midnight of 6 June.

illustrations.title: Required or not?
illustrations.q: Is an e-way bill needed? (a) A Delhi trader sends goods worth ₹45,000 to Noida; (b) a Pune company sends moulds worth ₹20,000 to a job worker in Gujarat; (c) a farmer moves fresh vegetables worth ₹2 lakh to a mandi; (d) goods worth ₹1,20,000 move on a hand cart within the city; (e) goods worth ₹80,000 move 40 km within Maharashtra from the supplier to a transporter's godown for onward inter-State dispatch.

head: Case
Needed?
Reason
rows: Inter-State movement to a job worker needs an e-way bill whatever the value
Fresh vegetables are listed in the Annexure to Rule 138(14)
Part A only; Part B not needed for the first leg
Movement up to 50 km within the State from consignor to transporter — Part B can be filled before the onward journey
solution.title: Rule 138

jobs.title: Dispatch desk checklist
jobs.situation: A factory's dispatch team asks when to generate e-way bills.
steps: Check consignment value excluding exempt goods.
Check special cases like job work and handicrafts.
Fill Part A; fill or delegate Part B.
Track validity and extend in time if delayed.
jobs.takeaway: Generate before movement; a late e-way bill does not cure detention.

mcqs.q: E-way bill is required where consignment value exceeds:
mcqs.explain: Rule 138(1) sets ₹50,000, measured on invoice value including tax but excluding exempt goods. In practice: special cases need it below this.
mcqs.topic: When an e-way bill is required (s. 68, Rule 138)

mcqs.q: Inter-State movement of goods worth ₹15,000 to a job worker:
options: Needs one only within the State
mcqs.explain: The principal or registered job worker must generate one for inter-State job-work movement regardless of value. In practice: use a delivery challan as the document.
mcqs.topic: When an e-way bill is required (s. 68, Rule 138)

mcqs.q: Validity for normal cargo travelling 250 km:
mcqs.explain: One day for every 200 km or part: 250 km needs 2 days. In practice: plan extensions for longer delays.
mcqs.topic: Who generates it, Parts A and B, and validity

mcqs.q: Part B of the e-way bill contains:
mcqs.explain: Part A has supply details; Part B has vehicle or transport document details. In practice: update Part B on transhipment.
mcqs.topic: Who generates it, Parts A and B, and validity

mcqs.q: An e-way bill can be cancelled within:
mcqs.explain: Cancellation is allowed within 24 hours if it has not been verified in transit. In practice: recipients have 72 hours to reject.
mcqs.topic: Who generates it, Parts A and B, and validity

mcqs.q: Which movement does NOT need an e-way bill?
options: Machinery in a truck worth ₹3 lakh
Inter-State handicrafts by an unregistered artisan
mcqs.explain: Non-motorised conveyance is exempt. The others need one. In practice: hand carts and bicycles are also non-motorised.

mcqs.q: Penalty to release taxable goods detained without documents, where the owner comes forward:
mcqs.explain: Section 129(1)(a) fixes 200% of the tax for an owner who comes forward; others pay the higher of 50% of value and 200% of tax. In practice: tax is paid separately.

mcqs.q: Part B need not be filled where movement within the State from consignor to transporter is up to:
mcqs.explain: Rule 138(3) proviso exempts Part B for intra-State movement up to 50 km between consignor or consignee and transporter. In practice: Part A is still needed.

questions.q: Compute e-way bill validity: (a) normal cargo moving 450 km; (b) over-dimensional cargo moving 70 km. The bill for (a) was generated at 10:00 am on 3 June. When does day one end?

model.text: A "day" ends at midnight of the next day after generation: the first day for (a) expires at midnight of 4 June, so validity of 3 days ends at midnight of 6 June.

mistakes: Counting the first day as 24 hours.

model.title: Rule 138

summary: Required above ₹50,000 consignment value (incl. tax, excl. exempt goods).
Below ₹50,000 still needed for inter-State job work and handicrafts by exempt persons.
Validity: 200 km/day; ODC 20 km/day; extension within 8 hours.
Cancel within 24 hours; recipient rejects within 72 hours.
Exemptions: Annexure goods, non-motorised, customs movements; Part B not needed up to 50 km.
traps: First day ends at midnight of the next day.
Exempt goods excluded from consignment value.

viva.model: Invoice value including GST, excluding the value of exempt goods on the same invoice.
The person who transports the goods — the registered supplier or recipient if using own conveyance, or the transporter.
By the generator within 8 hours before or after expiry, if goods cannot reach in time due to exceptional circumstances.
Goods moved by non-motorised conveyance and goods listed in the Annexure such as fresh vegetables, among others like customs-sealed movements.

viva.q: What happens if goods move without an e-way bill?
viva.model: They may be detained or seized under section 129 and released on payment of penalty, 200% of tax for an owner who comes forward.

cases.title: Swift Movers
cases.case: Swift Movers, a transporter, carries for a Bhopal manufacturer goods invoiced at ₹55,000 (including GST) plus exempt items of ₹10,000 on the same invoice, over 410 km to Jaipur. Midway the truck breaks down and the goods are shifted to another truck.

options: No, value after exempt goods is below ₹50,000
mcqs.explain: Consignment value excludes exempt goods: ₹55,000 of taxable goods including tax exceeds ₹50,000. In practice: show exempt goods separately.
mcqs.topic: When an e-way bill is required (s. 68, Rule 138)

mcqs.explain: 410 km needs three 200-km blocks (200 + 200 + 10). In practice: count part blocks as full days.
mcqs.topic: Who generates it, Parts A and B, and validity

options: Update Part B with the new vehicle number
mcqs.explain: Part B is updated whenever the conveyance changes. In practice: a new e-way bill is not needed.
mcqs.topic: Who generates it, Parts A and B, and validity

mcqs.q: If caught without a valid e-way bill and the owner comes forward, penalty is:
mcqs.explain: Section 129(1)(a): 200% of tax payable on the goods. In practice: pay to secure release.
